title: Security update check: newer chat server, Element web app and address search
security: Chat server (Synapse) moved to 1.164.0 and the Element web app to 1.12.33, which bring in newer image libraries (Pillow, certifi and others) with published security fixes.
Address search (Photon) moved from 1.0.1 to 1.3.0, which carries newer libraries; the existing address data keeps working with no new download.

title: Off-site copy right after the nightly backup (no extra backups), stuck copies close themselves, schedule look-up without a date, and clearer settings menu
improved: Admin menu: Site Settings is now General Settings and All Settings is All Settings (Everything), with a line on each page saying what it holds

Off-site copy: the small copy can start right after the nightly backup and send that same backup (the default), so nothing is dumped twice; a copy at a set time or by hand makes its own snapshot and removes it afterward (Off-Site Copy > Small Copy > When to Start)
Look It Up on a My Flights form shows airport names (with the code beside them in small type) instead of only codes, for the flights the receivers heard, the suggested route and the airline schedule
fixed: Off-site copy: a run that never reported back no longer shows as running forever (it is closed when the backup service restarts, after a few hours, or when you start another copy), and the database snapshot a small copy makes is removed when the copy ends instead of staying in Available Backups
Airline schedule look-ups say what went wrong (key refused, plan limit used, flight number or date not accepted, service unreachable) instead of one message for everything
Airline schedule look-up works without a date: it uses today's date
Flight Map: a flight with a recorded track is drawn only along its real path; the estimated straight line under it is gone (it stays only for flights without a track)

title: Off-site copy to a NAS over HTTPS (WebDAV) proven end to end, and the two-minute timeout on the first copy fixed
improved: Off-Site Copy over WebDAV is proven end to end: the certificate is always checked, copies go over https only, a big copy is streamed without being held in memory, and a failed Test the Connection says in plain words what is wrong (wrong password, no permission, folder missing, file too large for a proxy, out of space, certificate not trusted). The page shows the last successful small and big copy

Off-site copy: WebDAV over HTTPS is the first choice and the way to reach a NAS without opening port 22 (the duplicate NAS over SFTP choice is gone), the page explains the safe ways to reach a NAS, a web address given to SFTP or SMB and a plain http address are refused, errors from the destination are in plain language, and the last successful copy is shown
fixed: Off-site copy: the first copy no longer stops after two minutes while the database backup is made (the upload now waits for it), and a run the service never reported on is closed instead of showing 'running' forever

title: Find members in chat by call sign, the Chat button works for members who never opened chat, and radio bridges only on a member's own room
added: Chat finds members by call sign: every active member has a chat account (made ahead of time), and a member who allows being found by call sign carries it after their name in chat, so a search for the call sign finds them (Settings > Matrix Chat > Make a Chat Account for Every Member)
improved: Radio bridges: only the person who made a chat room can bridge it to an APRS call sign or mesh node; the standing rooms and other people's rooms cannot be bridged, and earlier links on such rooms are switched off
fixed: The Chat button on a friend or member who had never opened chat no longer says the profile could not be loaded: their chat account is made when you click it

title: Planefence shows its table again, chat points phones to the Element Classic app, and more code scanning fixes
fixed: Planefence and Plane-Alert show their table again: the script policy added in 1.8.2 had blocked the libraries those pages load, and they reported a stream error

Chat on a phone: the Chat page now names the Element Classic app (the newer Element X cannot sign in with a site account yet) and says how to sign in, and the chat web app no longer offers the phone app downloads
security: More of the code scanning review: the email, distance and place patterns that could be slowed by long input are replaced by plain checks, track files are read only by the safe parser, backup paths are checked against the backup folder, and links built in the satellite page are encoded

title: Code scanning review: tighter checks on the site address, track files, backups and typed input, and a two-factor QR code drawn by the site
security: Code scanning review: the Main Address check only contacts public addresses, track files (GPX and KML) are read by a parser that refuses entity tricks, a restore refuses a backup file that names a column the table does not have, backup and user names with a trailing line break are refused, and very long typed input is cut before it is matched
Two-factor set-up draws its QR code on the site itself, so the setup key is never handed to a script from another site

title: Matrix chat, My Flights (maps, sharing, schedules, tracks), a notification for every alert kind, mesh alert channel and linked areas, and a full security hardening
added: Chat and messages move to Matrix: end-to-end encrypted direct messages, group chats and rooms in the Element app and inside the site (Chat in the Community menu), signed in with your account. Reactions, replies, edits, pictures, files, voice messages, read receipts and typing notices all work. Old chats and messages stay where they are (closed); nothing was copied over

Notifications for chat: Element's own notices while the chat page is open (allow them once in its own window), and, from My Account > Community Settings, notifications on a phone or computer even when the site is closed (a new chat message shows who wrote it and, in a room that is not encrypted, the words)

Chat rules you control: who may start a room or a chat (everyone, friends or moderators), each member's own choice of who may contact them, blocks that hide a member's messages and invitations, moderators of the standing rooms (General, Aircraft, Weather, Radio and Help), reports and locks on Admin > Matrix Chat
The radio bridge works with chat rooms that are not encrypted (APRS and mesh nodes), and a standing room can be mirrored one way to a Discord channel
The Backups page opens at once however many backups there are (it no longer unpacks each one to count its rows); the chat database, keys and pictures are in the off-site backup
Admin has the same left side menu as My Account: groups that open and close, the page you are on marked, one button on a phone, and moving between admin pages without reloading everything

The first part of Matrix chat: the site can now sign members in to a Matrix server (Admin > Matrix Chat), so chat can move to end-to-end encrypted rooms that members reach with the Element app; nothing changes for members until it is switched on
Fixed: the page for one of your weather stations or sonde stations (My Account) could show an error

Search engines can find the site: robots.txt, a sitemap, descriptions and canonical addresses on the public pages, noindex on private pages, and boxes for the Google Search Console and Bing verification codes (Settings > Public Pages)
My Account opens on a new Overview page: what needs your attention, your profile, security, community and alerts at a glance, and a card for each kind of station you have

Mesh Channels can be combined: tick the default channel and any of your channels and get one QR code that adds them all to the Meshtastic app at once; the default channel has its own code, and each position choice shows about how far the position is blurred

Mesh Channels (Mesh menu > Mesh Channels, or My Account > Mesh Channels): make a private Meshtastic channel with a random key, get a QR code and an address for the Meshtastic app, and share it with chosen members, your friends or a chat group; they see the same QR code, and you can replace the key at any time

Mesh owner alerts: if you own a mesh node (a claim you completed, or a node on your mesh login) you are told when your router has gone quiet or its battery is low, and when it is back, by email, by your webhook and in a list on My Mesh Nodes; you choose what you hear about under Node Alerts

Verified Amateur badge: a member whose call sign was checked against the FCC records shows a badge and the call sign on their Profile, on a new member page (click a name in a chat or message), next to their name in chats and in messages
Radio panel inside every chat (under People and Settings) to link the chat to an APRS call sign or a mesh node, turn the link on or off and remove it, and a how-it-works box on the Chat page

Aircraft alerts can notify your phone or computer: tick Also Notify My Phone or Computer on an alert (turn notifications on first at My Account > Community Settings). Matches are combined into one notification, within limits the administrator sets
Mesh node alerts and friend requests can notify your phone or computer too (Node Alerts on My Mesh Nodes, and Community Settings; each is your choice)

Admin > Data Retention: every kind of stored data with its size and what happens as it ages, thinning of old weather readings, and removal of old chat pictures and files, with a dry run, a run log and a nightly run (nothing is thinned until you choose)

Mesh node pages chart the readings a node reports (battery, voltage, channel use, and any sensors: temperature, humidity, pressure, wind, rain, light), and Mesh Weather lists every node with sensors and its newest values
Mesh Router Planning: where one more router would help the most nodes that are poorly served today, worked out from what the network heard (a guide, not a coverage prediction)

Mesh Communities: each local mesh (Little Rock, Northwest Arkansas, Hot Springs and others) can have a page with how to join, its nodes on a map, news and events, and a team that runs it (Owner, Manager, Editor, Node Operator, Viewer, by invitation), with broker logins for its gateways

Remote administration of mesh nodes for a community: its Manager queues commands (read the settings, rename, role, channel name, reboot) that a small program on the group's own computer carries out, so the node's admin key stays with the group; changes wait for approval and everything is logged
The site reads the newest Meshtastic firmware and protobuf releases once a day, shows the firmware on Mesh Health, and tells the administrators when the packet formats may have changed
Download flight data when signed in: the flights on Flight History as CSV, KML or GeoJSON, and the track of one flight as CSV, GPX, KML or GeoJSON from its Flight Progress page
Mesh node pages and lists have a Where to Buy link for the node's hardware (an Amazon search); the administrator can add an Amazon Associates tag and exact product links later

Replay from the history pages: a Replay button on every Flight History row (and for the whole period) plays the flight back on the live map, and balloon flights can be replayed on the Radiosonde Map from the Balloon Flights list and each balloon's page, one at a time or several together

My Flights: a private diary of the flights you took (My Account > My Flights): pick the airports, write the times in each airport's own time (scheduled and actual for gate departure, takeoff, landing and gate arrival, or just a departure and an arrival), see taxi, air and total time and the distance worked out, and list who was on board with their seats

My Flights map and statistics: every route you flew on one map with airport circles sized by visits, and a statistics page with distance, time in the air, favorite airports, airlines and aircraft, longest and shortest flights and a year-by-year table
Replay on the flight page's own map (the aircraft's own icon, a trail, speed and slider) and on each balloon's page (balloon, launch flag, burst, parachute and landing icons)
The registration and flight number on a flight are links to every logged flight with them
Mesh communities can choose to show their nodes on the public mesh map and, if the site allows it, forward what their gateways send to the public Meshtastic server

My Flights: import and export as CSV, and Look It Up on the Add a Flight form, which finds the flight your site's receivers heard by flight number or registration and fills in the airports, aircraft and times
The Flights list and Flight History now show the same things: airline, aircraft make and model and the route, with the flight number and registration as links to every logged flight
My Flights fills in the airline, aircraft and the usual route from a flight number or registration as you type it
The radiosonde page replays on its own map with the same controls as the aircraft flight page
Guests no longer see the My pages, Mesh Channels or the sign-in-only parts of the About page, and every flight and balloon download needs a sign-in
Satellite Passes: Show on Map opens a map of just the satellites you ticked, with their paths and the part of the earth each can see
Planefence, Plane-Alert and the repeater code plug exports are for signed-in members only
The map selector no longer offers maps of services that are off or hidden from the viewer
The satellite map shows the place you entered and every pass of the ticked satellites over it in your look-ahead, with the rise, peak and set times

Feature Access: features that belong to a signed-in member (My Flights, chat, messages, friends, Matrix, radio bridges) now start as signed-in members only with wording that fits, and the Super Admin role always has access
My Flights can import a flight from a GPX or KML track with times
My Flights links a diary flight to the track and replay of the same aircraft when the site's receivers heard it
How to Feed is now an overview of everything you can feed the network, and the ADS-B instructions have their own page under the Feed menu
Mesh communities: members can ask to join a community's team, and its Managers approve or decline
The Mesh Map shows a crowd of nodes at one spot as one dot with a count, and spreads them out with their names in a column when you zoom in
My Flights imports an AirTrail CSV export

My Flights: every flight has its own page with its times, people and track; tracks (Flightradar24 KML, GPX) can be added to a flight, or imported in bulk where they attach to the matching flight; the flight map's airports and routes link to the flights
My Flights can pull everything (all the people and the tracks) straight from an AirTrail instance with an API key, or from an AirTrail JSON export
My Flights Flight Map draws the real recorded path of every flight that has a track, colored by height, and keeps the straight line for the others

My Flights can be shared by link: one flight or the whole diary (list, map and statistics), read only, no account needed, never listed by search engines; you choose whether the recorded track, the registration, the people and your notes show (people and notes start hidden), how long the link lasts, and you can remove it any time (My Account > My Flights > Shared Flights); administrators can switch sharing off and set the limits

Notifications page (My Account > Notifications): one switch for each kind of alert that can reach your phone or computer: chat, friend requests, community requests and news, aircraft alerts, mesh node alerts, someone opening a shared flight link, weather warnings, earthquakes and river flooding near your places, satellite pass reminders, landed balloons you follow, and (for administrators) items needing attention. The site can choose which kinds it offers and sets the limits
My Places: name places with a distance around each and get weather, earthquake, river and satellite notifications about them; Follow This Balloon on a balloon's page tells you when it lands

Airline schedules for My Flights: on the Add a Flight form, Look Up the Airline Schedule fetches the scheduled times, airports, airline and aircraft of a flight number on a date and fills the Scheduled column (needs the administrator to add an AeroDataBox key in Settings > Aircraft Lookups; answers are kept for a few days and every member and the site have limits)

Mesh alert and weather channel: a mesh community can choose one of its channels to carry National Weather Service warnings for its area and a weather summary from the weather stations inside it, out over the mesh to nodes that have downlink on (Alert Channel page of the community; the administrator switches it on for the site). The channel key stays in the site and the messages are encrypted before they reach the mesh service; there is a daily limit, a gap between messages, a test button and a log of everything sent

Linking mesh areas that no radio can join: a Manager of one community proposes a link on a shared channel, a Manager of the other accepts, a site administrator approves (Linked Areas page); the site then carries the channel's packets between the two communities' topics, still encrypted, once only, with a hop limit and a rate limit, and either side can pause or remove the link
Quiet hours for notifications: choose the hours when notifications are held back (urgent warnings can still come through if you allow it), on My Account > Notifications

The home page's Services section has a card for every service that is on (Repeaters, Mesh Nodes, ACARS, APRS, River Traffic, Drones, Satellites, Nets, the County and Trauma maps, and Chat for signed-in members), with its numbers and a link
improved: The Release Notes and Roadmap now come from the ArkSignal organization on GitHub (ArkSignal/ArkSignal-Content)
Chat, Messages and Friends are their own Community section; in My Account they are only settings and information (Community Settings: who can contact you, being found, blocked members)
Passkey errors now say what went wrong and what to check on a phone

My Account's pages are in a left side menu (a drop-down button on a phone), in collapsible groups (Account, Security, My Stations, Community Settings; the group you are in stays open, one open at a time) under one steady My Account header, and moving between them no longer reloads the page, instead of one long horizontal bar

Profile has private First name and Last name fields (kept encrypted, separate from the display name, never shown to anyone, not even administrators); your amateur license is now checked against them instead of the display name
Off-site backups: a NAS choice in Admin > Backups > Off-Site Copy walks through setting up a network storage box as the destination, step by step (it is sent over SFTP)
Profile shows your amateur license status with a Check Again button; My Account > Radio Bridges is now called Radio
Matrix sign-in no longer needs a return address typed in: it is worked out from the Matrix address

Mesh Communities: its own side menu with a page for each part (not one long page), an area drawn as a shape on a map and changed any time, a map for each mesh with nodes the team places by hand, its own topic on the broker with plain steps for connecting a gateway (uplink or uplink and downlink), and channels with QR codes that are public or only for chosen team roles
fixed: Mesh nodes refused again after the broker restarts (NOT_AUTHORIZED): the broker could not save the logins it was given because its config folder belonged to the wrong user, so they were lost whenever it restarted; the broker now takes ownership of its folder when it starts, and the site's automatic check puts back any login that is missing

Secrets are stored encrypted: the mesh broker password and the mesh gateway token are now sealed in the database, hidden on the Settings page and never written to the audit log; plain secrets left by older versions are sealed when the site starts (this pass had not been saving its work before)
Phone menu: a long section such as Aircraft now scrolls with the rest of the menu wherever you swipe, instead of only at the edge
The Admin backups page loads quickly again: it no longer opens and decrypts every backup file on each visit

Mesh broker logins no longer need pressing Apply after an update: the site checks every couple of minutes that the broker holds every member's login and sends any that are missing, so a rebuilt or reset broker never leaves your node refused (NOT_AUTHORIZED)
Mesh nodes whose hardware showed only as a number now show its name; the mesh service also reads the Meshtastic project's list of hardware once a day so new models name themselves
My Flights: importing an AirTrail export whose tracks carry numeric times no longer ends in an error
Moving to the Flight Map (or another My Account page that loads a library) with the side menu no longer says the map library did not load until the page is refreshed
security: A script policy for every page: only the site's own scripts (each marked with a one-time code) run, inline event handlers are gone, and popups on the maps clean any text that came from outside, so injected script does nothing

Sign-in answers the same way for an unknown name, a wrong password, a disabled account and a locked one, and takes the same time; a new sign-in starts a fresh session; changing or resetting a password ends the account's other sign-ins; passwords longer than 256 characters are refused
Password reset, community invitation and shared flight links are built from the site's own address, not from the address a request claims

Requests from visitors and receivers are limited to 10 MB (a member's flight import 40 MB, the admin area more); the web server's log no longer holds secret addresses (receiver upload addresses, reset and invitation links); signed-in pages are not cached by browsers

Webhook and AirTrail addresses are connected to only after one check of where they point (no changing answers), including shared 100.64 addresses; email passwords are never sent unencrypted and plain email only goes to a server on your own network

The mesh, ACARS, APRS, prediction and Matrix helper services can require a shared token (SERVICE_TOKEN in the stack's .env), and Admin > Overview tells you when it is not set or the SECRET_KEY is short; the public-server mesh password is stored sealed

Private message text (the old messages and chats) is stored sealed, backup files and the backup folder are private to the portal's user from the first byte, and the mesh service keeps its broker passwords sealed

The private flight diary is stored sealed too: the notes on a flight and the names of the people who flew are encrypted in the database and opened only for you, a person a flight is shared with, or your own export

title: Updates now come from the GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io/arksignal) as well as Docker Hub
improved: Updates now come from the GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io/arksignal/arksignal-*) as well as Docker Hub: the services' bundled compose files, the installer script and the update check use the new names, and the update check can read either registry (Settings > Scheduled Updates)

title: The new address arksignal.net, finding members by call sign or email, claim a mesh node, mesh broker protection and Neighbor Info links, GOES viewer improvements, public source code
improved: Friends, chats and messages: type a user name, a call sign or a whole email address to find a member (a list of matches appears as you type, several names with commas for groups and messages); the email address is never listed or shown, and each member can switch off being found by call sign or email on My Account > Friends
Mesh: every node's page has a Claim This Node button for signed-in members (you get a code to put in the node's name), and says when a claim is waiting or the node is yours

Mesh broker protection: the site's mesh broker follows the public Meshtastic server's rules on the public channels (only the allowed kinds of packet are kept, and a position more exact than 16 bits is made coarser before it is stored), members' logins can publish only under the site's own topic root, and the broker refuses oversized messages and limits connections; four settings control it

Settings > General: a new Main Address or Feed Address is checked before it is saved (it must resolve in DNS, and the Main Address must answer over https as this very site), so a wrong name can never lock everybody out of the site; the site publishes its own identifier at /.well-known/arksignal.json for this check
The site's own address moves to arksignal.net: the feed pages show feed.arksignal.net, the "already feeding" note is gone, and the old site names only redirect to the new one
fixed: The MQTT server name on How to Feed the Mesh Map no longer shows the text <wbr> between its parts
Mesh nodes standing at the same spot no longer cover each other on the Mesh Map and the overview map: they fan out in a ring with thin lines to the true place

title: Live chat, email-style messages and friends, radio bridges, GOES viewer with loops, mesh overview and Neighbor Info, API keys and passkeys, new data layers
added: County Map: a Limit To box in Show on the Map limits every kind of point (and the drive-time rings) to one state, one county, or the area around a ZIP code or place; it is kept in the link to the view

My Account > Display and Maps: every Display menu choice (theme, decorations, page width, clock, time zone, units for each service, aircraft map choices) and your saved map views (open, rename, delete) in one place, with a reset; the Trauma Map's views can be saved too

Call Sign Lookup: type the start of a call sign (KD5) and every call sign on the site that begins with it is listed, with what each is (repeater, APRS station, station owner, sonde receiver, DMR contact)

Weather Alerts layer: the National Weather Service's active warnings, watches and advisories drawn as colored areas on the maps (tornado red, severe storm orange, flood green, winter pink, heat, fire weather, wind); click one for the details. Admin > Settings chooses the states and how often it refreshes

Earthquakes layer: recent earthquakes in and around Arkansas (the New Madrid zone) from the USGS, as circles sized and colored by magnitude; click one for the time, depth and the USGS page. Admin > Settings chooses the area, smallest magnitude and days back

River Gauges layer: river and lake gauges in and around Arkansas from NOAA's National Water Prediction Service, as dots colored by flood category (green no flooding up to purple major flooding); click one for the stage, flow and the NOAA page. Admin > Settings chooses the area
Radio > Space Weather: NOAA's storm scales, planetary K index with a three-day chart, solar flux, X-ray flare class and a rough HF band guide
Weather panel: NOAA Visible Satellite and Water Vapor imagery under Satellite, and a Lightning layer (strike density) under Alerts and Hazards

Feeder achievements: friendly badges (Long Reach, Furthest Reach, Always On, Busy Antenna, Veteran, Established, New Arrival, Network Pillar) on the Feeders page and each feeder's page, worked out from the real numbers, with an Achievements section that says what each takes and who holds it; every limit is a setting

Kiosk Display (Display menu): a wall-screen mode that shows pages full screen with no menus, with an Exit Kiosk button (and Esc), a Setup panel to choose the pages, how long each stays up, a preset or a single page only, a bar that hides itself when nobody is touching the screen, and a link that keeps the setup; presets and the default pages are settings. Any page also works without menus when its address ends in ?kiosk=1; the date and time can be drawn on the screen at a chosen corner and size (settings), and the menus, panels and map controls of a kiosk page (and the kiosk's own bar) hide after a set time with no input and come back with any input
Trauma Map: one switch, Air ambulance aircraft, shows every helicopter and airplane on the air ambulance lists that the network hears right now, with a details card and a Legend entry

API keys and a documented public API: members make a key per project on My Account > API Keys (shown once, only a fingerprint kept), and a key opens /api/v1 (aircraft, feeders, weather stations, radiosonde flights, repeaters) with fair per-minute and per-day limits that every answer reports; the API page (Network menu) explains getting started, the endpoints, the limits, the errors and the rules of use; administrators see, limit, revoke, restore and make keys for members on Admin > API Keys (a new Manage API Keys permission), everything is in the audit log, and the limits are settings; administrators can switch single API endpoints off on Admin > API Keys > Endpoints (or in Settings > API): an endpoint that is off answers 403, is not counted against any key, and is marked on the API page

Passkeys: sign in with your fingerprint, face, screen lock or a security key instead of a password. Add passkeys on My Account > Passkeys (name them, rename, remove; synced and device-only ones are marked), and choose Sign In with a Passkey on the sign-in page: no user name or password, and because the device checks it is you, it stands in for the password and the two-factor code together. Only the public half is kept; the challenge, origin, site address, signature (ES256, RS256, EdDSA), user verification and use counter are all checked, and a counter that goes backwards (a copied passkey) is refused and logged. Administrators can see a member's passkey count and remove them for a lost device; the limits and the verification rule are settings

Send your weather station to the APRS network: on a weather station's page the owner can switch on sending its newest reading, about every ten minutes, as an APRS weather report to CWOP (the Citizen Weather Observer Program, which feeds NOAA) or APRS-IS (amateur radio, with the owner's own call sign). It needs the owner's consent that the readings and the position are public, sends the position the site shows (or the exact one if accepted), has a Preview the Report and a Send Now button, shows the last result and a count, and is logged; administrators see which stations send and can manage them like the rest of the station page. The interval, servers and the call-sign check are settings

Radio > Satellite Passes: when the space station, the weather satellites and the amateur radio satellites (SO-50, AO-91, AO-92, RS-44, FO-29, AO-7 and more, chosen in Settings) rise over a place you type, a ZIP code, an airport or your own location: the time, which way to look, how high they climb, how long they are up, a small sky chart of each pass, what is overhead right now and notes on what to listen for. The orbit data is read from CelesTrak once a day by a new Satellite Orbits job in Data Updates

Radio > Nets and Radio > Winlink Gateways: two directories kept by the network's own members. Nets shows each net's schedule in plain words (every Tuesday, the 2nd Thursday, the last Sunday, every day, irregular), when it next happens in your own time zone (daylight saving handled), a coming-up-this-week list, what to tune to and who runs it, with filters by day, mode and text. Winlink Gateways lists the call sign, mode, frequency, place and notes, and sorts them by distance from a place you type. Members add and keep their own on My Account > My Nets and Gateways; editors check new entries before they show (a setting), and administrators and editors manage every entry, can add one for a member, and everything is in the audit log

Our own NOAA GFS data: the prediction service now reads the Global Forecast System weather model itself, a new cycle every six hours cut to a box around Arkansas (winds at 26 heights and the surface forecast), instead of depending on a middleman. The balloon wind predictor flies the balloon through these winds (Automatic: ours while fresh, else Open-Meteo; or ours only, or Open-Meteo only), and Weather for a Place has a new Hour-by-Hour Model Forecast: temperature, humidity, wind, gusts, three-hour rain, cloud and pressure every three hours for three days, in your units. Admin > Radiosondes shows the cycle and has a Read the Newest GFS Cycle Now button; the area, hours and schedule are settings

Satellite Passes now answers how to work each satellite: an open section above the passes lists the uplink and downlink frequencies, the mode and access tone, whether a license is needed to transmit, what equipment it takes and a note, and every pass shows the downlink and how far the Doppler shift moves it from rise to set

A Satellites layer on every map: where the space station, weather and amateur radio satellites are right now, with the path each takes in the next 45 minutes and the part of the earth it can see; click one for its height, speed, the next pass over the map center, its frequencies and what it takes to work it
API: an endpoint an administrator switches off disappears from the API page and the endpoint list, and a new setting lets an administrator make API keys only (members then ask for one)

Satellite Images: members with a weather satellite receiver (Meteor-M, GOES or NOAA) add it on My Account > My Satellite Receivers, get a private upload address and send their decoded pictures to it; the pictures show on Radio > Satellite Images with the satellite, the receiver and the time, linked to Satellite Passes. Administrators manage receivers and pictures on Admin > Satellite Images

GOES Imagery: the newest pictures from NOAA's GOES-East and GOES-West weather satellites on Weather > GOES Imagery, for Arkansas and the Mississippi Valley, the Southern Plains and the whole country, in GeoColor, infrared, water vapor, air mass and red visible views; kept fresh by the site itself and credited to NOAA

Sign in with Google: members can link a Google account on My Account > Google Sign-In and sign in with one click; it stays hidden until an administrator enters the Google client ID and secret on Admin > Google Sign-In

How to Feed Satellite Pictures: a new feeding page with an uploader script for members who decode weather satellite pictures, a section on sending a weather station's readings to the APRS network on the weather feeding page, and every feeding page now lists all the others automatically; Am I Feeding? shows satellite receivers too

River Traffic: towboats, barges and boats on the rivers and lakes, heard by members' own AIS receivers, on a list, a map, a page for each vessel and a Marine Traffic layer for every map; members add a receiver on My Account > My AIS Stations and follow How to Feed AIS (a small bridge program sends what the receiver decodes), and administrators can add stations and hide a vessel on request

Drones: aircraft that broadcast Remote ID, heard by members' own receivers, on a list, a map, a page for each drone and a Drones layer for every map; members add a receiver on My Account > My Remote ID Stations and follow How to Feed Remote ID. The operator's location is never stored unless an administrator turns that on
